author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Build a touchscreen layout for portrait testing
summary: Create a separate portrait diagnostic layout, respect cutout and gesture insets, preserve the PS2 viewport, test combinations, and prove rotation does not overwrite landscape.
heroAlt: PCSX2 hotkey configuration representing a separate compact control set prepared for portrait diagnostics

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals

blocks.text: Treat portrait as a separate diagnostic workspace

Start from a separate portrait preset and capture the phone's usable rectangle after the status bar, camera cutout, navigation gesture strip, and emulator toolbar are visible. Choose a game scene that exercises both sticks, shoulder buttons, Start, and rapid face-button combinations. Place diagnostic controls around that measured rectangle instead of scaling the landscape overlay by a percentage.

Never overwrite the everyday landscape preset while exploring portrait placement. A control can remain visible yet sit inside Android's back-gesture edge, behind a cutout, or outside a comfortable thumb arc. Keep at least one route to the emulator menu accessible so a bad overlay cannot trap the session without a way to restore the saved layout.
Map the portrait safe and reachable regions

items: Landscape layout exported and named independently.
Display cutout plus gesture areas visible in portrait.
One test scene that uses both sticks, shoulders, and face buttons.
Capture portrait and landscape screenshots with cutout, gesture, toolbar, and viewport boundaries visible before moving a control.
Exercise two sticks, a shoulder hold, and two face-button taps in the same portrait scene to expose reach and multi-touch cancellation.

blocks.text: Place groups from the safe edges inward

items: 1. Rotate before editing and confirm the app reports the final portrait bounds.
2. Reserve a stable viewport area for judging PS2 output.
3. Place D-pad and left stick within the lower supporting-thumb arc.
4. Place face buttons and right stick within the opposite reachable arc.
5. Keep Start, Select, shoulders, and diagnostic actions separated from gestures.
6. Test two-button chords and stick-plus-button actions with both hands.
7. Rotate to landscape and confirm its saved layout remains unchanged.
8. Return to portrait after app restart and verify every control stays inside safe bounds.

blocks.text: Use the touch visualizer to distinguish reach problems from multi-touch cancellation. Hold one stick at a diagonal, press a shoulder button, and tap two face buttons in succession. If a contact disappears only near an edge, move that element inward; if the same combination fails anywhere, reduce overlapping hit regions or check the device's supported touch count.
Accept a rotation-safe portrait test layout

Rotate portrait to landscape and back, background the app, and reopen the same game. The portrait preset should return with every control inside the current safe area, while the untouched landscape preset retains its original coordinates. Capture both orientations with the touch indicators enabled so later UI or inset changes have a comparable reference.

items: No control intersects the camera cutout or gesture exclusion edge.
The PS2 viewport remains large enough for visual diagnosis.
Portrait and landscape profiles preserve independent geometry.
Compare annotated screenshots after rotation so movement of a control can be separated from a changed Android safe area.
Relaunch directly into portrait, rotate twice, and verify that both orientation presets return to their saved coordinates.
Controls move after rotation: save under an orientation-specific profile.
Shoulders cannot be held with a stick: reposition groups before shrinking targets.
The viewport is hidden by controls: reserve it first and rebuild outward.
System back triggers during play: move the conflicting target inward.

blocks.text: Return to the preserved landscape geometry

Switch explicitly to the saved landscape preset, verify it, and only then delete the experimental portrait layout. If the menu becomes unreachable, use Android's app restart rather than clearing all application data. A failed portrait experiment should remove one overlay file, not controller profiles, game settings, memory cards, or library permissions.
Portrait is best treated as a diagnostic layout

Portrait is useful for one-handed diagnostics and narrow-device testing, but many PS2 games require simultaneous controls that remain more practical in landscape. Recheck the layout after display-size, font-scale, gesture-navigation, or cutout-mode changes because Android can alter the safe rectangle without changing the physical screen.
